reasons: Snooze is hidden on phone-sized screens with no other option shown.
The menu button on completed reminders has no action.
No tests are visible in this file.

terms.meaning: a function the parent passes in, which runs when something happens

sections.name: File setup, ReminderType
sections.title: Imports and reminder types
sections.what: Brings in icons, the card and button parts, and a helper for joining style names. It also defines the four reminder kinds: medication, water, meal and sleep.
sections.why: The four kinds decide which icon and colors each reminder gets.
sections.watch_out: Adding a new reminder kind requires a matching entry in the style table below, or the card will fail to find its style.

sections.name: Reminder
sections.title: Shape of one reminder
sections.what: Describes the data for one reminder: an id, its kind, a title, a sub line, a time, and a status of pending, completed or snoozed.
sections.why: Gives the card a fixed set of fields, so the page passing data in knows what to provide.

sections.name: typeStyles
sections.title: Colors and icons for each reminder kind
sections.what: Maps each reminder kind to its icon and its background and text colors, such as a blue water drop and a purple moon for sleep.
sections.why: Makes the four kinds easy to tell apart at a glance.

sections.name: ReminderCard (part 1)
sections.title: Reminder card layout and completed look
sections.what: Shows one reminder as a card with an icon, title, kind label, time and sub line. When the reminder is completed, the card fades slightly, shows a check mark and crosses out the title.
sections.why: Shows at a glance what is due and what is finished.
sections.watch_out: The completed style is decided only by the status value, so the card will not update until the parent passes a new status.

sections.name: ReminderCard (part 2)
sections.title: Snooze and Done buttons
sections.what: For pending reminders, shows a Snooze button (desktop only) and a Done button. For completed reminders, shows a menu icon instead. The buttons call the actions passed in from the parent page.
sections.why: Lets the user mark a reminder finished or postpone it. The desktop-only Snooze button is likely to keep the phone layout simple, but the code does not state this.
sections.watch_out: The card does not do the work itself. Snooze and Done only fire the callbacks from the parent, so if the parent does nothing, nothing is saved. The menu icon on completed reminders has no action attached.

summary: A single row showing one reminder (medication, water, meal or sleep) with Snooze and Done buttons.
purpose: Lets a patient see a due reminder and mark it done or delay it.
why: Likely reason: each reminder type gets its own icon and color so it is easy to recognize. The look for completed items is not explained in the code.
how: Picks an icon and colors from the reminder type. When the reminder is not complete, it shows Snooze and Done. When complete, it shows a check mark, a struck-through title and a menu button. The real completing and snoozing happen in the callbacks passed in by the parent.
inputs: A reminder with id, type, title, subtitle, time and status, plus the onComplete and onSnooze callbacks.
outputs: A visual row. It calls onComplete or onSnooze when a button is clicked, and does not store data itself.
risks: Snooze is hidden on small screens with no visible alternative. The menu button on completed reminders has no action.
debug: If a reminder shows the wrong icon, check its type value. If buttons do nothing, check that the parent passes callbacks that update the reminder's status.
